title: Lines of symmetry
keyIdea: A line of symmetry is a fold line: fold the shape on it and one half lands exactly on the other. On squared paper, a mirror line reflects each square to a partner the same distance from the line, on the other side, so a square next to the line stays next to the line. A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry, not 4, because folding on a diagonal does not make the corners meet. Mirror lines can be vertical, horizontal or diagonal.

kid: Fold a shape in half. If the two halves match exactly, the fold is a line of symmetry. We also call it a mirror line.
Some shapes have more than one. A square has 4. A rectangle has only 2. Fold a rectangle corner to corner and the corners do not meet.

To finish a shape on squared paper, count each square from the mirror line. Its partner is the same number of squares away on the other side. A square that touches the line has a partner that touches it too.
Do not slide the half across. A mirror flips it. And the mirror line can lie flat or slant, not just stand up.
adult: In England, Year 4 pupils identify lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes presented in different orientations, and complete a simple symmetric figure with respect to a specific line of symmetry. Year 2 meets line symmetry in a vertical line first. In the US, Common Core 4.G.A.3 defines a line of symmetry as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts.

The key fact is distance. A reflection keeps every point the same distance from the mirror line, measured straight across at a right angle to it. On squared paper with a vertical line, a square 2 columns to the left lands 2 columns to the right, in the same row. With a diagonal line from corner to corner, the row and column numbers swap.

Common mistakes to watch for: saying a rectangle has 4 lines because the diagonals look like they cut it in half; sliding the given half across instead of flipping it; counting from the edge of the grid instead of from the mirror line; and reflecting straight across when the mirror line slants. Folding paper or using a small mirror checks each one.

In the lab you fold a rectangle on four lines and see which two work, then shade squares to complete figures across a vertical, a horizontal and a diagonal mirror line. Wrong squares turn red and the feedback names the slip.

familyTip: Fold a sheet of paper in half, cut out a shape along the fold and open it: the fold is a line of symmetry. Then hunt at home for shapes and letters with 0, 1, 2 or more lines.

visual.caption: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry? Drag each one, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: fold a rectangle to find its lines of symmetry, then complete figures on squared paper across vertical, horizontal and diagonal mirror lines.

practice.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
practice.hint: Fold it corner to corner in your head. Do the corners meet?
practice.explain: 2: across the middle and up and down. The diagonals do not work because the corners do not meet.

practice.prompt: A shaded square is {d} squares to the left of a vertical mirror line. How many squares to the right of the line is its reflection?
practice.hint: Count from the mirror line, not from the edge of the grid.
practice.explain: A reflection keeps the same distance from the mirror line, so it is {d} squares to the right, in the same row.

practice.prompt: The mirror line runs between columns 5 and 6 of a grid. A square is in column {c}. Which column is its reflection in?
practice.hint: Find how far column {c} is from the line, then go the same distance past column 6.
practice.explain: Column {c} is {=6-c} columns left of the line, so its reflection is in column {=11-c}.

practice.prompt: Mia copies the left half onto the right half without flipping it. What has she done?
choices: She slid it, so it is not a reflection
practice.hint: Does a square next to the mirror line stay next to it?
practice.explain: Sliding moves every square the same way. A mirror flips the half, so squares near the line stay near the line.

pool.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
pool.hint: Count the straight folds and the corner to corner folds.
pool.explain: 4: up and down, across, and both diagonals. All four folds make the halves match.

pool.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
pool.hint: It has 3 equal sides. Try a fold from each corner.
pool.explain: 3: each fold goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side.

pool.prompt: Which capital letter has a horizontal line of symmetry?
pool.hint: Fold across the middle. Do the top and bottom match?
pool.explain: B: its top and bottom halves match. A has a vertical line instead, and F has none.

pool.prompt: Half a symmetric shape has {n} shaded squares, and none of them touch the mirror line. How many squares does the whole shape have?
pool.hint: Each square gets one partner on the other side.
pool.explain: {n} squares and {n} partners make {=2*n} squares in the whole shape.

pool.prompt: A square touches a vertical mirror line on its left side. Where is its reflection?
choices: Touching the line on the right side
At the right edge of the grid
One square away from the line
pool.hint: How far from the line is the square?
pool.explain: It is 0 squares from the line, so its partner touches the line on the other side.

pool.prompt: A horizontal mirror line runs between rows 4 and 5. A square is in row {r}. Which row is its reflection in?
pool.hint: Count how many rows row {r} is above the line, then go that far below row 5.
pool.explain: Row {r} is {=4-r} rows above the line, so its reflection is in row {=9-r}.

pool.prompt: A diagonal mirror line goes from the top-left to the bottom-right corner. The square in row 1, column 4 reflects to which square?
pool.hint: With this diagonal mirror, the row and column numbers swap.
pool.explain: Row 1, column 4 becomes row 4, column 1. Flipping straight up or down is the slip.

pool.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a slanted parallelogram with no right angles, and long and short sides, have?
pool.hint: Try each fold. Do the corners ever meet?
pool.explain: 0: no fold makes the halves match, not even corner to corner.

pool.prompt: Tom says mirror lines are always up and down. Is he right?
choices: No, they can go across or slant too
pool.hint: Think of the letter B and the square folded corner to corner.
pool.explain: No. B has a horizontal line, and a square has 2 diagonal lines of symmetry.
